key_insight: AI agents could deepen inequality when people differ in whether they can access agents, how capable those agents are, and how many they can use. This paper offers a conceptual framework for identifying these risks and a research agenda for addressing them.
problem_solved: Clarifies how unequal access to AI agents—and differences in their quality and number—could create societal inequalities.
method: Develop a conceptual framework for understanding agentic inequality.
Identify potential sources of inequality linked to agent access, quality, and quantity.
Propose a research agenda to investigate and address these societal risks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the framework highlights why evaluating agent capabilities alone is not enough: who can access and deploy those capabilities also matters. It encourages attention to distributional effects when designing and deploying AI agents.
visual_elements: Three-axis diagram showing access, agent quality, and number of agents as dimensions of inequality.
Side-by-side illustration of people with no agents, one basic agent, and multiple capable agents.
Conceptual flowchart linking unequal agent resources to potentially unequal societal outcomes.
Research roadmap graphic connecting risk identification, investigation, and responses.
paper_authors: Matthew Sharp, Omer Bilgin, Iason Gabriel, Lewis Hammond
